description_full: Gates Industrial Corporation Ltd. manufactures and sells engineered power transmission and fluid power solutions in the United States, rest of North America, South America, the United Kingdom, Luxembourg, rest of Europe, the Middle East, Africa, India, East Asia, and Greater China. It operates through two segments, Power Transmission and Fluid Power. It offers solutions for stationary and mobile drives, engine systems, personal mobility application platforms; elastomer drive belts; asynchronous and synchronous belts, V-belts, transmission belts, and micro-V belts; metal drive components, such as tensioners, idlers, pulleys, sprockets, mechanical water pumps, and other accessories used in belt drive systems; and kits for the automotive replacement channel. It also provides fluid power solutions for stationary and mobile hydraulics, vehicle systems, and other industrial application platforms; hydraulics comprising hoses, tubing, couplings, and fittings, as well as assemblies; thermal and emissions management and related products; and industrial hoses, including data center pumps. Its products are used in diversified industrial applications comprising automated manufacturing, logistics systems, and data centers; consumer applications of printers, power washers, automatic doors, and vacuum cleaners; industrial off-highway, such as construction and agriculture; industrial on-highway commercial vehicles, including heavy-duty trucks and buses; energy and resources markets, such as oil, gas, and mining; and personal mobility, including scooters, motorcycles, bicycles, all-terrain vehicles, and snowmobiles. It sells its products under the Gates brand. It offers its products to aftermarket channel customers and original equipment manufacturers. Gates Industrial Corporation Ltd. was formerly known as Gates Industrial Corporation plc and changed its name to Gates Industrial Corporation Ltd. in July 2026. The company was founded in 1911 and is based in Denver, Colorado.

financial_summary: Gates Industrial Corporation Lt is a mid-cap industrials business with a $6.1B market cap on $3.4B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at -1% over the past three years — essentially flat, and a business treading water is rarely a path to compounding.
Returns on capital run at 8% against a 9% cost of capital, which means the business is destroying value with every dollar it reinvests, with gross margins sitting at 38%.

The business throws off $405M in free cash flow — roughly 12 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 1.90× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, debt is moderate at 2.1× net debt/EBITDA, serviceable in normal conditions but worth watching through a downturn, and interest coverage runs at 3.7×.
Shareholder yield is only 1.8%, a thin return of capital, and insider ownership is negligible, so management has little personal stake in the long-term outcome.

growth: Revenue has compounded at -1.1% over 3 years and 4.3% over 5 years, so growth is decelerating.

Free cash flow has compounded 10.1% a year over five years.
Capex runs only 0.3x depreciation (2.1% of sales), so the asset base is being harvested rather than grown.
Its Rule of 40 score is 15, below the 40 that marks a healthy growth business.
own: Insiders own a modest 2.0%, and reported institutional holdings exceed 100% of shares (a sign of heavy share lending).
Shareholder yield is a modest 1.8% (1.8% in buybacks).
The share count has shrunk 3.0% a year over five years, steadily raising each holder's stake.
people: With about 13,000 employees, each generates about $265K of revenue, 0.7x the Industrials median, and productivity has risen 4.3% a year.
That works out to $31K of free cash flow per employee.
CEO pay is $3.2M (12x revenue per employee), and compensation governance scores well (3/10, lower is better).
